title: [Bugfix] Make Attention Backend Auto-Selection Batch-Invariance-Aware (#40193)
linked_issues: #40173 Automatically select highest priority batch-invariant attention backend
body:
Fixes #40173

Makes attention backend selection batch-invariance-aware, enabling auto-selection of the highest-priority backend that supports batch invariance when none is explicitly specified. Specific changes:

* Adds `supports_batch_invariance()` to `AttentionBackend`, defaulting to `False`.
* Adds `is_batch_invariant` to `AttentionSelectorConfig`.
* Updates `validate_configuration()` to reject backends that do not support batch invariance when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`.
* Marks `FLASH_ATTN`, `TRITON_ATTN`, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA`, and `TRITON_MLA` as batch-invariant-capable.
* Defers backend compatibility validation when no backend is explicitly set, so selector-based auto-selection can run before validation.
* Preserves clear runtime errors for explicitly selected unsupported backends.
* Adds batch-invariance check to the Mamba backend selector path, so unsupported Mamba backends are rejected when VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1.

title: [NVIDIA] Add sm_110 (Jetson Thor) to CUDA 13.0 build targets (#39233)
body:
## Summary

- Add compute capability `11.0` (`sm_110`, Jetson Thor) to all `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` configurations that feed CUDA 13.0+ builds
- The official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.0-cu130` image ships **without** `sm_110` kernels, making it completely unusable on Jetson Thor — precompiled CUDA kernels for Marlin (GPTQ-INT4), CUTLASS (`cutlass_scaled_mm`, FP8), and flash-attn (BF16) all fail with `CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device`
- For CUDA < 13.0 builds, the CMake `cuda_archs_loose_intersection()` in `CMakeLists.txt` safely filters `11.0` out since it is not in `CUDA_SUPPORTED_ARCHS` for those toolkit versions

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `docker/Dockerfile` (2 locations) | Added `11.0` to default `torch_cuda_arch_list` ARG |
| `.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml` (5 locations) | Added `11.0` to all CUDA 13.0 wheel + release image builds |
| `tools/flashinfer-build.sh` | Added `11.0` to CUDA 13.0+ FlashInfer AOT arch list |

## Context

`cuobjdump -lelf *.so` inside each image shows:

| Image | Architectures |
|-------|--------------|
| Official cu130 | sm_87, sm_89, sm_90, sm_100, sm_120 — **no sm_110** |
| Jetson Thor image | sm_90, sm_110, sm_120, sm_120a — **has sm_110** |

Note: `CMakeLists.txt` already includes `11.0` in `CUDA_SUPPORTED_ARCHS` for CUDA >= 13.0 — it just was never requested via `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST`.

title: Support only half types for concat_mla_q kernel (#37892)
body:
## Purpose

This PR fixes `concat_mla_q` kernel for float32 dtype

* Currently in `concat_mla_q` kernel, `q_pe` is casted to int* (4 bytes), so `ld32_cs` loads the rope section in 32 * 4 = 128 bytes, see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.18.0/csrc/concat_mla_q.cuh#L50-L55. This works correctly if DType is bf16 or half, because 64 rope elements take 64 * 2 = 128 bytes
* However, if DType is float32, 64 rope elements take 64 * 4 = 256 bytes. So it copies only first half of the rope data. Therefore, instead of copying rope data once, it needs to copy in 2 iterations.

A key characteristic of mimo v2 flash architecture is that the attention layer uses different head dimensions for keys and values (v_head_dim != head_dim)

title: [Attention][TurboQuant] Share dequant buffers, eliminate float16_copy (#40941)
body:
# TurboQuant Backend Optimizations

**Builds on top of**: shared-decode-buffer PR (#40655)

## Summary

Backend-level optimizations for the TurboQuant KV cache attention backend, reducing memory usage and improving prefill latency for long-context workloads.

**Key results** (L4 TP=4, GPTQ-Int4 + TQ k8v4):
- **Saves 57 GB memory at 1M context** — shared dequant buffers via WorkspaceManager in the **continuation prefill path** (60× reduction; the earlier PR #40655 shared buffers in the decode path only)
- **Eliminates float16_copy kernel** in decode (stage2 OUTPUT_FP16) — removes redundant copy after stage2 reduction
- **Enables CUDA Graph capture for continuation prefill** — the old per-layer `_tq_k_dequant_buf` grew lazily on first long request (triggering cudaMalloc inside a captured graph crashes); WorkspaceManager pre-allocates at profiling time so buffer addresses are fixed during replay
- **Fixes output_buf dtype mismatch** in shared-buffer decode path
- **117 existing TQ unit tests pass**

## Changes

### Memory Optimizations

**1. Shared dequant buffers via WorkspaceManager** (P0 — critical)

`_continuation_prefill` allocated per-layer FP16 dequant buffers (`_tq_k_dequant_buf`, `_tq_v_dequant_buf`) that grew to the max continuation length seen. With 60 active TQ layers × 2 buffers, memory grew with O(layers × context_len):

| Context | Per-layer (old) | Shared (this PR) | Savings |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8K | 480 MB | 8 MB | 472 MB |
| 32K | 1.9 GB | 32 MB | 1.87 GB |
| 128K | 7.5 GB | 125 MB | 7.4 GB |
| 1M | 58.6 GB | 976 MB | **57.6 GB** |

Fix: Use `current_workspace_manager().get_simultaneous()` to allocate dequant buffers from the shared workspace pool. This ensures:
- Buffers are shared across all layers (workspace is global per ubatch)
- Buffer sizes participate in GPU memory profiling (correct KV capacity calculation)
- **Required for CUDA Graph capture** — per-layer growth pattern is incompatible with CG (buffers must be fixed-size at capture time)

The shared-decode-buffer PR (#40655) already shares the decode-path buffers (`mid_o_buf`, `output_buf`, `lse_buf`) via WorkspaceManager in `_decode_attention`. This PR extends the same pattern to the **prefill/continuation** dequant buffers — different buffers in a different code path.

### Prefill Optimizations

**2. Remove redundant `.zero_()` on dequant buffers**

The `_tq_full_dequant_kv` kernel writes all positions up to `cached_len`, and we only read `[:cached_len]` afterwards. The trailing positions are never read. Removing `.zero_()` eliminates 2 memset kernels per layer per continuatio …[truncated]

title: [Attention][Spec Decode] Allow independent drafter attention backend selection (#39930)
body:
## Purpose

Currently, when running with speculative decoding, the drafter's attention backend is pegged to be identical to that of the target model. This is problematic when these have incompatible requirements (e.g. MLA vs GQA) or the drafter has restrictive requirements (e.g. DFlash, which requires non-causal support).

This PR adds `--speculative-config.attention_backend` (analogous to `--speculative-config.moe_backend`) to allow independent specification.

Unlike `--moe-backend`, though, if only `--attention-backend` is passed, the drafter will not inherit the target's backend because incompatibilities are common -- it will be auto-selected.

If neither `--attention-backend` nor `--speculative-config.attention_backend` is passed, the two backends will be auto-selected independently.

### Behavior matrix

| `--attention-backend` | `--speculative-config.attention_backend` | Target backend | Drafter backend |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | (none) | auto-select | auto-select |
| `X` | (none) | `X` | auto-select |
| (none) | `Y` | auto-select | `Y` |
| `X` | `Y` | `X` | `Y` |

## Test Plan

On A100, run
```
vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-speculator.dflash \
    -tp 2 \
    --attention-backend <target> \
    --speculative-config.attention_backend <drafter>
```

Fails with:

```

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Size arange_buffer to max_num_batched_tokens to prevent CUDA IMA (#39277)
body:
Hi from [novita.ai](https://novita.ai/) team 👋

## Purpose

Fix a CUDA illegal memory access (IMA) crash in the MLA indexer's decode flattening path when using data parallelism + speculative decoding (MTP).

### What changed

`arange_buffer` in `DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder` was allocated with size `max_num_seqs * next_n`, while the other flattening buffers (`expanded_seq_lens_buffer`, `expanded_block_table_buffer`) correctly use `max_num_batched_tokens`. During CUDAGraph dummy runs on idle DP groups, stale `query_start_loc` entries for padded requests inflate `actual_expanded` beyond `max_num_seqs * next_n`, causing a silent out-of-bounds GPU write.

### Why

1. `execute_dummy_batch` creates a 1-request dummy batch but `_build_attention_metadata` uses `num_reqs_padded` (CUDAGraph bucket size).
2. `query_start_loc` is only populated for the 1 real request; padded indices retain stale values from previous real batches.
3. `split_decodes_and_prefills` classifies all padded requests as decodes (since `max_query_len <= decode_threshold` with spec decode).
4. The flattening path computes `actual_expanded = sum(decode_lens)` over all padded requests, yielding values far exceeding the buffer size.
5. `self.arange_buffer[:actual_expanded]` writes out-of-bounds → CUDA IMA surfacing asynchronously at the next sync point.

## Test Plan

Tested with GLM-5-FP8 on 8× H200:
```bash
vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5-FP8 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative-config.method mtp \
  --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 3 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
```

## Test Result

- **Before fix**: Server crashes with CUDA IMA soon under load (1000 requests, avg 10K prompt tokens)
- **After fix**: Server ran 85+ minutes stable under the same benchmark load with zero errors

title: Add nvfp4 kv cache support (#40177)
body:
This is a follow up of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37332 to fully enable nvfp4 kv cache using flashinfer trtllm backend.
This builds on the existing NVFP4 infrastructure (packed layout, `reshape_and_cache_flash` kernel, `KVQuantMode.NVFP4`) and wires up the read/attention side so that end-to-end NVFP4 KV cache inference works through FlashInfer on Blackwell (SM100).

Key changes:

- **FlashInfer backend**: Add `"nvfp4"` to `supported_kv_cache_dtypes`. Force `trtllm-gen` backend for both prefill and decode wrappers when using NVFP4 KV cache, since FA2/FA3 do not support NVFP4. Set `o_data_type` to FP8 in wrapper `plan()` calls because the NVFP4 trtllm kernel only supports FP8 output.
- **FP8 output handling**: The NVFP4 trtllm-gen kernel only produces FP8 output. When the model dtype is not FP8, a pre-allocated FP8 buffer (`_nvfp4_fp8_out`) is used and results are dequantized back to the model dtype. This applies to all four code paths (prefill wrapper, prefill trtllm, decode wrapper, decode trtllm).
- **Block scale forwarding**: Pass `kv_cache_sf` (split from the packed NVFP4 KV cache via `nvfp4_kv_cache_split_views`) to the FlashInfer wrapper `run()` and `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` calls.
- **Rename `get_fp8_dtype_for_flashinfer` to `get_dtype_for_flashinfer`**: Now also handles `"nvfp4"` -> `torch.uint8` mapping.

title: [Bugfix] Fix degenerate KV cache stride causing TMA cudaErrorIllegalInstruction (#40737)
body:
## Purpose

Fix cudaErrorIllegalInstruction → NCCL allgather hang → EngineDeadError that occurs when num_kv_heads_per_rank == 1 (e.g. Qwen3.5-397B with --tensor-parallel-size 8) and prefix caching is enabled.

Root cause: When prefix-cached KV blocks are freed and reallocated, PyTorch can produce tensor views with a degenerate stride on the singleton num_kv_heads dimension. is_contiguous() returns True for any stride on a size-1 dimension, so .contiguous() does not fix it. CUDA TMA (used by FlashInfer XQA SM90 and Flash-Attention 3/4 on H100+) requires all non-outermost strides to be multiples of 16 bytes; a bf16 stride=1 (2 bytes) violates this and faults.

This bug affects all three attention backends:
  - FlashInfer (flashinfer.py): degenerate stride at dim -3 of kv_cache_permute after permute(), shape [..., num_kv_heads=1, block_size, head_size]
  - FlashAttention (flash_attn.py): degenerate stride at dim -2 of key_cache after unbind(0), shape [num_blocks, block_size, num_kv_heads=1, head_size]
  - FlashAttentionDiffKV (flash_attn_diffkv.py): same dim -2 issue after the packed [..., head_size_k + head_size_v] last-dim slice

Fix: Add canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides() to vllm/utils/torch_utils.py. Uses torch.as_strided to patch size-1 dim strides to their canonical C-contiguous values — zero-copy, only stride metadata is updated. Safe because a size-1 dimension is never stepped across in pointer arithmetic (0 × stride = 0 regardless of stride value). Applied in all three backends immediately after the KV cache tensor is sliced for reading.

Also tightens the existing TRTLLM stride assertions in flashinfer.py to include stride(-3) so any future regression on SM100 surfaces with a readable error rather than an opaque CUDA fault.

## Test Plan

Unit tests (no GPU required — pure PyTorch metadata operations):

PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kv_head_stride_canonicalization.py -v

Integration reproducer (requires H100, TP=8, model with 8 total KV heads):

```

    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --attention-backend flashinfer  # or flash_attn
  ## Send two requests with a shared prefix. Second request sometimes triggers
  ## block reallocation → degenerate stride → crash without this fix.
```

Workaround confirmation: Setting VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN on older vLLM versions still crashes (both backends are affected). The fix resolves both. Disabling prefix caching is the other workaround for getting rid of this crash.

title: [Model Runner V2] Rebuild attn metadata between draft decode steps (#41162)
body:
## Context
Investigating DSV4 "invalid memory access" crash that happens when MTP > 2. I believe that crash is caused by not rebuilding the attention metadata in between draft decode steps. DSV4's attention metadata builders have position-dependent state that must be updated whenever the position is advanced. For example: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e9f8f31e9a4c31d6842ca1adffe2619ed204fafb/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py#L293-L307.

During draft decoding, we only update the sequence lengths, positions, and slot mappings, but not the metadata properties dependent on those: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e9f8f31e9a4c31d6842ca1adffe2619ed204fafb/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/speculator.py#L316-L327.

Any attention backend with builders that have position-dependent state can potentially be affected by this bug.

## This PR
Fixes the above issue by rebuilding attention metadata in between draft generation steps during the multi-step decode loop. Because attention metadata building is not guaranateed to be a cudagraph-compatible operation, we must capture the single-step draft generation, and replay in each iteration of the loop. The captured draft generation routine consists of the following operations, in order:
1. `run_model` - Draft model forward pass to get hidden states.
2. `compute_logits` - Computes logits from hidden states.
3. `_sample_draft` - Samples a draft token using either gumbel or greedy sampling (depending on what was configured)
4. `update_eagle_draft_inputs` - Updates the output draft tokens (`self.draft_tokens`) for the current step, and updates the inputs for the next draft step, such as input ids, hidden states, positions, etc.

title: [ROCm][DeepSeek] Enable V3.2 TP4 AITER MLA (#41835)
body:
## Purpose

This PR enables the remaining DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4-specific pieces needed for ROCm AITER MLA serving.

DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 reaches local MLA `num_heads=32`. Current ROCm AITER MLA rejects that head count through `_AITER_UNSUPPORTED_HEADS = [32]`, so the model can fail before reaching the HIP graph accuracy path with `unsupported head_num: 32`. This PR removes that stale block now that the AITER-side MLA kernel support for this shape exists.

This PR also preserves DeepSeek's fp32 MoE correction bias when `GateLinear.out_dtype` is unset. The previous fallback cast `e_score_correction_bias` to the gate weight dtype, which can lose routing precision for DeepSeek's biased grouped top-k path and contribute to wrong expert routing or incoherent output.

This is the DeepSeek-specific split from Frida Andersson's original draft PR #41760. The shared ROCm AITER HIP graph replay fixes were split separately into #41816. This PR intentionally does not duplicate those graph replay changes. The full DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 HIP-graphs fix is expected to require this PR plus #41816, along with an AITER build that includes `num_heads=32` MLA kernel support.

Special thanks to Frida for the original investigation, patch direction, and DeepSeek-V3.2 validation. This PR is a minimal split of her DeepSeek-specific work so it can be reviewed independently from the cross-model graph replay fix.

title: Use CU_MEMCPY_SRC_ACCESS_ORDER_ANY for batch KV cache swaps (#39306)
body:
Use `CU_MEMCPY_SRC_ACCESS_ORDER_ANY` instead of `CU_MEMCPY_SRC_ACCESS_ORDER_STREAM` in the `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` call used for batched KV cache swap copies.

This relaxes the source access ordering constraint, allowing the CUDA driver to pipeline reads more aggressively. The safety of this change relies on the fact that source data is always fully written before the batch copy begins — the offloading handler synchronizes via stream events (`stream.wait_event(last_event)`) before issuing the copy.

Motivated by [this code review comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38460#discussion_r2120927236) from @ivanium on PR #38460, who observed improved CPU->GPU bandwidth on Grace Blackwell nodes with `ACCESS_ORDER_ANY`.

title: [ROCm] Cap Triton paged attention block size to fix ROCm shared memory OOM (#38502)

Hybrid Mamba models (e.g. Jamba) inflate block_size to 2048 to align attention and Mamba page sizes. ## Purpose

When I did an nsys profile of DSv4 prefill, several memory-bound kernels show up as taking quite a bit of time. Now

title: Triton attention: add USE_TD constexpr for tensor descriptor Q/K/V load/store (#40327)
body:
## Summary

Add an optional tensor-descriptor (TD) load/store path to the Triton
unified attention kernel in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py`.
The TD path uses `tl.make_tensor_descriptor` for Q/K/V loads and the
output store, which enables HW 2D block reads on Intel Xe2/Xe3.
The non-TD branch is preserved and stays bit-for-bit identical — both
`USE_TD` and `USE_TD_QO` are `tl.constexpr` so the dead branch is
eliminated at Triton compile time, giving zero overhead when disabled.

This PR rides on top of the 2D/3D kernel unification in #40631; the
new TD helpers mirror that structure.

## Changes

### `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py`

- Three new module-scope TD helpers: `_load_q_td`, `_load_kv_tile_td`,
  `_store_output_td`. The output helper is **shared between the 2D
  and 3D epilogues** — they differ only in base pointer and
  `(stride_token, stride_head)`.
- `kernel_unified_attention` gains `USE_TD` / `USE_TD_QO` constexpr
  parameters and a `tl.static_assert(BLOCK_SIZE % TILE_SIZE == 0)`
  guard under `USE_TD`.
- Q load, K/V tile load, and the 2D and 3D output stores each pick
  the TD or pointer path at compile time. The KV-load branch fetches
  its physical block index via a scalar `tl.load` (safe because every
  slot in a KV tile shares the same block under the static-assert
  guarantee).

### `vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py`

- Auto-enable TD on XPU only (`self.use_td = current_platform.is_xpu()`
  when the env var is unset). Other platforms stay on the pointer
  path by default.

### `vllm/envs.py`

- Register `VLLM_TRITON_ATTN_USE_TD` as **tri-state**:
  - unset (default) → platform auto-select (XPU on, others off);
  - `"1"` → force TD on regardless of platform;
  - `"0"` → force TD off regardless of platform.
  Useful for A/B-ing the TD path on the same device.

### `unified_attention()` wrapper

- New `use_td: bool = False` kwarg, passed through from the
  `triton_attn` backend.
- `TILE_SIZE_PREFILL` / `TILE_SIZE_DECODE` clamped down to
  `block_size` when `use_td` is set, so the static-assert holds for
  the common `block_size=16` configuration without surprising users.
- `USE_TD_QO` is gated on both `is_pow2(num_queries_per_kv)` **and**
  `HEAD_SIZE == HEAD_SIZE_PADDED`. When either is false (e.g.
  Qwen2-7B: `28/4=7`, or Phi-3-mini: `head_size=96`), Q load and
  output store fall back to the pointer path; KV tile loads stay on
  TD because their `block_shape` does not involve those axes.
- Python-side asserts `q.stride(1) == head_size` and
  `out.stride(1) == head_size` whenever `USE_TD_QO` …[truncated]

title: [Bugfix] Fix TRTLLM ragged MLA prefill workspace warmup (#42112)
body:
## Purpose

Fix `TRTLLM_RAGGED` MLA prefill failing after CUDA graph capture.

After the MLA prefill backend refactor in #32623, the FlashInfer workspace used by `TRTLLM_RAGGED` MLA prefill is allocated lazily. The first real request after `lock_workspace()` could hit:

```text
Workspace is locked but allocation from 'trtllm_ragged.py:66:_get_workspace_buffer' requires 394.00 MB, current size is 0.00 MB. Workspace growth is not allowed after locking.
```

Eagerly allocate the FlashInfer workspace buffers during MLA prefill backend initialization so they are reserved before `lock_workspace()`.

cc @MatthewBonanni @LucasWilkinson @mgoin

## Test Plan

Run the server with `TRTLLM_RAGGED` MLA prefill on GB300 GPUs:

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --attention-config.mla_prefill_backend TRTLLM_RAGGED \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k2 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k2 \
  --speculative-config '{"model": "lightseekorg/kimi-k2.6-eagle3-mla", "method": "eagle3", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```

## Test Result

Before this PR, the command above did not start successfully and failed with the locked workspace assertion.

After this PR, the same command starts successfully and works correctly with `TRTLLM_RAGGED` MLA prefill.
